explanation: Begin at the top-right corner. If that value is too large, discard its column; if too small, discard its row. Sorted rows and columns make each discard safe.
timeComplexity: O(r + c). Each failed comparison removes one row or one column; at most r+c moves occur.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only row and column indices are stored.

correctness: At the top-right of the remaining search rectangle, a value larger than x rules out its whole column because values below are no smaller. A value smaller than x rules out its whole row because values to its left are no larger. Each move removes only impossible cells, so finding equality or exhausting the rectangle is conclusive.
walkthrough: For [[1,4,7],[3,6,9],[5,8,12]] and x=8, start at 7: move down to 9, then left to 6, then down to 8. Equality proves the target occurs, so return true.
edgeCases: An empty matrix or zero-column matrix returns false.
Rows and columns must both be nondecreasing.
Repeated values do not invalidate the elimination argument.
Each move discards a row or column, giving the stated linear bound.
